entities.summary:
The President of the European Parliament is a public office in the European Union, established in 1958 as part of the European Economic Community. This office has played a crucial role in shaping the EU's legislative agenda, with key figures like Alcide De Gasperi, Robert Schuman, and Jean Monnet driving the project's early years. The President has been instrumental in promoting European integration, with notable milestones including the signing of the Maastricht Treaty in 1992 and the establishment of the EU's single currency, the euro, in 1999. The office has also been at the forefront of addressing pressing issues like climate change, migration, and economic inequality, with the current President, Roberta Metsola, leading efforts to strengthen EU-Russia relations and promote a more inclusive and diverse European Union.

The President of the European Parliament has significant influence over the EU's legislative process, with the power to set the agenda and shape the debate on key policy issues. The office has also been a key player in shaping the EU's relations with other global powers, with notable achievements including the establishment of the EU's Global Strategy in 2016 and the launch of the EU's Africa Strategy in 2017. The President has also been instrumental in promoting EU citizenship and the rights of EU citizens, with notable initiatives including the EU's Citizenship Directive and the EU's Freedom of Movement policy.

The legacy of the President of the European Parliament can be seen in the ongoing efforts to strengthen European integration and promote a more inclusive and diverse European Union. The office has played a crucial role in shaping the EU's response to major crises like the COVID-19 pandemic and the Russian invasion of Ukraine, with the current President, Roberta Metsola, leading efforts to promote a more united and resilient EU.
